comment.text: Arcade drive with held wheel speeds (rpm). Your ArcadeS function is on the right. Give the robot about a metre of room and press the board button. Expect: forward, a gentle left curve, a spin on the spot, full forward (1 + 1 is scaled back to 0.5 + 0.5, so this is a hard curve, not faster), then stop. Below it is a greyed-out better version, "arcade rpm", with its own test stack; see its comment to switch over.

comment.text: Your ArcadeS function, block for block. Straight and Turn run from -1 to 1; 1 means MaxSpeed rpm. Both 0 releases the speed hold, which stops the wheels without braking.

Better version (switched off). What changes: fwd pct and turn pct are percent, -100 to 100, like the arcade drive block; values past 100 are clamped; anything under 5% counts as 0 so joystick jitter does not creep the robot; max rpm is an input instead of fixed inside; the inputs are never overwritten (the scaling goes into its own variable). Variable names differ from ArcadeS because Blockly treats Turn and turn as the same variable. To use it: right-click this block and choose Enable Block, do the same on the test stack below, then drag that test stack under the start block in place of the ArcadeS calls.
